intro: The fifty-fifth screen read 138 pictures, the set's 21 and 117 probes, with eighteen readers and six scorers: 1,442 of 1,458 scored items had full marks, and none was misread. **All 64 templates pass the legibility gate**, as in v0.57, and 63 of them read 1.00. **`square_wheel`, at 0.967 in v0.57, reads 1.00 in eleven pictures**, six of them wheelbarrows that a grown figure wheels; the garden that had the two half marks is in full. **`seesaw_heavy`, at 1.00 in v0.57, reads 0.967:** one reader of five gave the man's weight and left open whether the child is stuck. It is the one item of an event under full marks; the other fifteen are the clouds or a tree that a reader left out. Nothing was mended, swapped or read again after the screen, so the count is the first and only one. The set's score is 0.982, for 0.971, and each of its five items under full marks is the clouds. Two of the changes are the scorers' and not the pictures': `carry_bag` and `paint_fence` read 1.00 for 0.938 and 0.958 because a man called a boy now costs nothing by rule, and the strict count has a narrower flag. With the 3 full marks that stand beside another reading in the description itself halved, all 64 pass; with the 58 that have another reading only in the reader's unsure section halved as well, which is what v0.57 counted, 55 pass, for 54. In the 113 pictures that came back from v0.57 to the pixel, 1,136 of 1,175 items have the score they had, and 37 of the 39 others are the clouds or a tree. The grown figures are called by a young name first in 7 of their 124 pictures, for 5 of 117.
design:
## Design tests

There were none of new pictures in v0.58 (`vision/design_tests_v058.md`). Every rule and drawing of revision 52 was read where v0.57 already had a picture, in that picture built again on its own record's plan, which is what the two benches are. Three pictures were not read before the screen: the tier-4 garden, whose set changed, and the two probes that were added for the wheeled barrow. All three read in full but for the clouds, which the readers of the garden and of one probe left out.

No picture of the set or the probes was built again after a reading.
screen:
Across all 138 pictures 1,442 of 1,458 scored items had full marks, and none was misread (v0.57: 1,391 of 1,435). Of the 16 under full marks:
- fifteen are setting items that four readers left out, thirteen the clouds and two a tree, all zeros (v0.57 had forty, from eight readers). One reader left the clouds out of six of its seven pictures;
- one is the heavy seesaw's inference, a half mark: "The man sits on the low end, which rests near the ground, and the girl is up on the raised end holding the handle, which fits the heavier person being lower."

The set's headline is all items 0.982 (0.971 in v0.57). Of its 277 items five are under full marks, the clouds in five pictures (things 0.953). Actions, inferences and contradictions read 1.00.

**After the screen.** Nothing was changed: no probe or isomorph was swapped and no picture was read again. The list for v0.59 is `vision/flaws_v058.md`.

**What was mended, in the screen.** The six wheeled barrows read in full: the square wheel is wrong or impossible in the description of four ("The odd thing is the wheelbarrow: its wheel is drawn as a square with an X/spokes inside rather than a round wheel, which would not roll."), a little odd with a hedge in one, and only in the unsure section in one. The kite in the tree reads 1.00 in six pictures with a hedge in three, as many as before: "it could also be read as flying just in front of the tree, but it overlaps the branches and the string is slack and looped on the ground, which suggests stuck." The heavy seesaw's man is on his seat to every reader, and none has him keep her up on purpose; its child is flagged in all five pictures, and in two she is not said to be stuck. The plain seesaw and the game of catch read 1.00 with no flag and no oddity.

**A second reading of 113 pictures, and a first of 22.** In the 113 pictures that are v0.57's to the pixel, 1,136 of 1,175 items have the score they had, 33 are higher and 6 lower; thirty-seven of the 39 are the clouds or a tree, and the other two are the men called boys, half marks then and full marks now by the rule. In the 22 that were drawn again or moved, 219 of 228 matched items have the score they had, six are higher and three lower: six of the nine are the clouds or a tree, two are the wheelbarrow's contradiction items in the garden that had the half marks, and one is the heavy seesaw's inference (`tools/cycle/retest.py`).

**The cast in the descriptions.** The scorers wrote a word under `who` for seven actions in six pictures: a man called a boy four times and a woman called a girl three times. By the first inventory line that names each figure's clothes, the count of every screen since v0.49, the four grown figures are called by a young name first in 7 of their 124 pictures, for 5 of 117 in v0.57: the man in the red shirt in 4 of 29, the woman in purple in 3 of 29, the woman in the yellow dress in none of 34 and the man in green in none of 32. The two counts agree. The man in the red shirt is a boy eating an ice cream, painting the fence, carrying a shopping bag and looking into the hose's nozzle: "In the centre, a boy or young man in a red T-shirt and blue jeans is walking to the left with a yellow shopping bag." His moustache is in his line in 6 of his 29 pictures (6 of 26 in v0.57), and the beard of the man in green in 20 of his 32 (14 of 30).

**What the full marks rest on.** The scorers flagged 70 full marks as judgement calls, for 67 in v0.57. In 3 the description or the inventory sets another reading beside the target: the floating box twice and the frying pan once. In 58 the description gives the target plainly and another reading is offered only in the unsure section, where the reader is asked for two readings of anything. In 9 a near word or a target partly said was credited. With the 3 halved all 64 templates pass; with the 3 and the 58, which is what v0.57's one flag took in, nine templates are under 0.9 and 55 of the 64 pass (54 in v0.57); with all 70 halved, 54 pass (51). The six scorers flagged 10, 15, 15, 10, 7 and 13, so the counts compare only roughly.

**Oddities and remarks.** The scorers logged 20 oddities in the 138 pictures, 0.1 a picture for 0.3, and one of them in the set for 12; the prompt's sentence on oddities is unchanged, so the fall is the scorers' and the readers' as much as the pictures'. The readers' remarks were 2.37 per picture (2.47). What the oddities are about: a goat tethered in a park and its rope, four times in three pictures; the wind that moves a cap and not a swing, a book's pages or the washing, three times in two; water at the hose reel, twice; a sprinkler's spray that lands short of a wet box, twice by one reader; and singles, one of them new: a kite's string that passes close behind the head of the barrow's pusher. No oddity is about a seat on the seesaw, the kite's reel or the barrow's handles.
redrawn: `square_wheel` reads 1.00 in eleven pictures, for 0.967 in ten; `seesaw_heavy` 0.967 in five, for 1.00; `kite_in_tree`, `seesaw`, `play_catch`, `sitting_on_air` and `pan_watering` read 1.00, as they did. `carry_bag` and `paint_fence` read 1.00 for 0.94 and 0.96 by the scorers' new rule and not by a drawing. It is one screen, of 8 to 33 items a template in this table, and a half mark moves a mean by 0.02 to 0.06.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (11 in three, 11 in four, 16 in five, 14 in six, 5 in seven, 3 in eight, and one each in eleven, twelve, sixteen and twenty-two). All 64 pass, as in v0.57; 63 did in v0.56, v0.55 and v0.54. The count is the first and only one, with no fix and no re-read behind it. One template is under 1.00, `seesaw_heavy` (0.967 on fifteen items in five pictures); the other 63 read 1.00. Per angle (`vision/v058/gate_yaw.json`), all (template, angle) pairs pass. The pass count rests on the scorers' rule as they applied it. Two of the 63 owe their 1.00 to a change of that rule (a man called a boy costs nothing now). And with the 61 full marks halved that stand beside another reading anywhere in a description, 55 of the 64 pass: the nine that fall are inferences and contradictions that a reader gives as the likelier of two readings (the floating box, the upward water, the fork, the stopped hose, the thief bird, the heavy seesaw, the begging dog, the fish and the kite in the tree). The gate is a filter, and the pilot with people is the test of difficulty.
inspection: Fifteen of the sixteen cells were carried over from v0.57's records, on their seeds with their templates (`tools/cycle/carry_over.py`): thirteen to the pixel, and two with the kite's child drawn again. The tier-4 garden is replaced. Its set of nine, forced on its seed since v0.53, held the wheelbarrow with a square wheel and placed on none of twelve seeds once a grown figure wheels it (five parked): the cell is the same set with the man who sits on nothing in the barrow's place, on the same seed (`tools/cycle/forced_cell.py`, `v058garden`). The tier-4 park, street and playground are v0.57's to the pixel. All five isomorphs are v0.57's, four to the pixel and the tier-4 garden's with the kite's child drawn again. Of v0.57's 115 probes all came back under their names, 96 of them to the pixel and 19 drawn again or moved; two probes were forced for the wheeled barrow (`tools/cycle/extra_probes.py`): 117 probes. **I looked at the 24 pictures that changed or are new on contact sheets before any reader had them, and at the tier-4 garden whole; I found nothing to mend and built none again after that look.** All 138 records rebuild identical to the pixel, and the library passes the validator in full, 427 of 427.
calib: The calibration measured with the new cast under revision 52 (`calibration.json`) moved in 6 of its 252 numbers by 0.002 or more, all the square wheel's, whose barrow is larger in the hands of its pusher. **The priors were left at v0.56's** for the second release, so that the planner draws v0.57's plans and the set stays like for like: by the new calibration five would move a little (`square_wheel`'s salience from -0.03 to 0.03, `kite_in_tree`'s from -0.73 to -0.74, `windy_hat`'s from -1.28 to -1.32, `ducks_bread`'s from -1.34 to -1.36, and `seesaw_heavy`'s distance term by 0.003), and `pan_watering`'s prior still has no second cue. A record's own predicted difficulty is computed from its layout, as always. A release that builds a new set should take them (`tools/cycle/calib_cmp.py`, `set_prior.py`).
